purpose: Reference gathering for the Atomic Acres Nuke Town Rebuild arena (nuketown2). Companion to docs/research/2026-09-04/R4-bo2-nuketown-accuracy.md.
primary_target: Black Ops 2 'Nuketown 2025' (version tag BO2-2025). Every other version is SECONDARY and is used only where a BO2-2025 image agrees.

version_tags.BO2-2025: Call of Duty: Black Ops II, map 'Nuketown 2025' - THE TARGET
version_tags.BO7-2025: Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 re-release of Nuketown 2025 - secondary
version_tags.BO1: Call of Duty: Black Ops, the original Nuketown - different map, control only
version_tags.CW-84: Black Ops Cold War, Nuketown '84 - different map, control only
version_tags.BO6: Black Ops 6 Nuketown - different map, control only

download_note: All files fetched with curl from static.wikia.nocookie.net. Fandom's CDN content-negotiates to WebP by default; '&format=original' was appended to every image_url at fetch time to get the true PNG/JPEG. Only image bytes were downloaded; nothing executable.

images.what_it_shows: Black Ops 2 in-game minimap for Nuketown 2025. Orthographic top-down of the playable volume: two house footprints at opposite ends of the LONG axis, street between them, circular turning head visible mid-street with two vehicle capsules on it, a rectangular arm off one side of the circle (the road stem) and an angled closed boundary opposite. Stylised glow render, so footprint edges are soft.
images.used_as_evidence: YES - question 4 (aspect + lollipop cul-de-sac). Too soft to settle garage ends on its own.

images.what_it_shows: Near-vertical aerial of the whole Nuketown 2025 site. Shows the lollipop cul-de-sac (circular turning head plus a straight stem running off-map), the coach and the box moving truck parked on the head, a dark saloon beside the truck, a green classic car out in the stem, both team houses flanking the road, the third (dark pitched-roof) house with its own drive and red car beyond the head, both back yards with their dressing, and the east house exterior stair and rear deck.
images.used_as_evidence: YES - questions 1, 3 and 4. Strongest single overhead in the set.

images.grade: press / preview capture of first-party content
images.what_it_shows: Elevated view from INSIDE one team back yard looking at that team own house - the exact viewpoint the owner question 1 describes. Butterfly / swooping roof, terracotta-orange upper walls over a cream ground floor; wooden EXTERIOR STAIR rising to a railed REAR DECK on the LEFT end; GARAGE WING with three dark barrel-vault bays on the RIGHT end; circular concrete patio at the stair foot; yard dressing (glasshouse and cold frames, curved-roof carport, crate store, stepping stones, hedges); road, coach and cars beyond the house. Only 640x345, but unambiguous at that framing.
images.used_as_evidence: YES - the decisive image for question 1 and for question 3 on the orange house.

images.grade: press / fan capture of first-party content
images.what_it_shows: In-map gameplay frame, 2560x1440. Player stands under a DEEP FLAT OVERHANGING EAVE / porch canopy above a concrete deck, firing across a mown yard bounded by a timber fence, a brick-based hedge run and scalloped hedging, with mannequins and a large orange curved-glazed out-of-bounds building beyond.
images.used_as_evidence: PARTIAL - question 3 (porch canopy over the front entry). NOT used for house colour: the yellow surface at frame right could not be tied to a specific team house.

images.what_it_shows: Load screen showing the site ENTRANCE, outside the playable area: the Nuketown pylon sign (Discover the City of the Future), a geodesic dome, an observation tower, a Futuro-type saucer house, the cream and maroon Nuketown coach, a hydro-car on a display plinth, a mannequin and barrier gates.
images.used_as_evidence: YES - establishes the art brief (retro-futurist model town, NOT the BO1 desert tract housing) and the coach livery.

images.what_it_shows: End-of-match nuke over the same entrance plaza. Second read of the Nuketown pylon sign, the entrance barrier, hedges, the hydro-car plinth with its readable placard and a mannequin.
images.used_as_evidence: PARTIAL - corroborates NT05 on entrance dressing; no layout content.

images.what_it_shows: Greetings From 2025 postcard art: the Nuketown tour coach in cream and maroon at close range, the pylon sign, a flag line and a mannequin.
images.used_as_evidence: PARTIAL - coach livery and proportions only.

images.what_it_shows: The playable-console easter egg: a period TV cabinet with atomic-motif wallpaper, a POPULATION counter, a mannequin, stone cladding and lawn behind.
images.used_as_evidence: NO layout content. Kept for interior and prop dressing.

images.what_it_shows: Map tile / key art: a bullet-holed fallout-trefoil sign reading NUKETOWN 2025 in orange on dark blue.
images.used_as_evidence: NO geometry. Kept for signage palette.

images.what_it_shows: 4096x4096 Black Ops 7 minimap of Nuketown 2025. Crisp white playable area, red hatched out-of-bounds, grey building footprints. Both houses read clearly as a main block plus an attached wing, with the two wings on OPPOSITE ends (a 180-degree rotational pair, not a mirror pair). Street channel with three vehicle bodies; a bay protruding at one end of the street (the turning head) and a straight fenced boundary with posts at the other.
images.used_as_evidence: YES - the clearest footprint evidence in the set, but SECONDARY: it is the BO7 re-release. Used only where the BO2 aerial (NT02) agrees.

images.what_it_shows: Street-level render from the cul-de-sac. The ORANGE house frontage with a steep swooping gable, orange infill panels in cream mullions, and TWO GARAGE DOORS at grade with a red classic car in the open bay; the silver and maroon tour coach; a blue-teal box truck; a Welcome to Nuketown board; a pale yellow-green out-of-bounds showroom at frame right.
images.used_as_evidence: SECONDARY - corroborates that one team house is orange and that its garage opens onto the street.

images.what_it_shows: A character standing ON an upper-floor REAR DECK - timber decking, orange top rail on white balusters - looking down over that house back yard: hydroponic planter racks, a glasshouse, stepping stones, a pool or water feature below the deck, hedges, and the out-of-bounds town beyond.
images.used_as_evidence: SECONDARY - shows the rear deck as a real standing and firing position at upper-floor height.

images.what_it_shows: The OTHER team back yard at ground level: a white / cream rounded modernist house with blue trim at frame left, the white-and-blue Nuketown GARDEN POD on the lawn, a sand pit with a swing set, a timber back fence with a HOLE punched through it, hedges, and a lime and teal panelled out-of-bounds showroom (See the homes of the future) behind the fence.
images.used_as_evidence: SECONDARY - ties the garden-pod and sand-pit yard (seen in the BO2 aerial NT02) to a WHITE / CREAM house, and shows the fence hole.

images.what_it_shows: A large TV-set prop (Experience the year 2025, POPULATION counter) on a lawn; a yellow classic car on a drive; a pale yellow-green low building with a long window band and roof solar panels behind; mannequins; the saucer tower and an observation tower.
images.used_as_evidence: SECONDARY - dressing only; the yellow-green building could not be tied to a team house.

images.grade: fan capture of first-party content (spectator camera)
images.what_it_shows: ORIGINAL Black Ops 1 Nuketown from the spectator camera: a fenced desert test township of many small 1950s tract houses - a YELLOW house, a TEAL / GREEN house, a PINK house and a PALE BLUE house - with a YELLOW SCHOOL BUS and an orange fire truck in the road, an army truck, mannequins, and scrub desert beyond the fence.
images.used_as_evidence: YES, as a NEGATIVE CONTROL: it shows that the yellow-and-green (and yellow-and-blue) house pairing belongs to BO1 Nuketown, not to BO2 Nuketown 2025.
